name: Greater Houston
metroName: Houston-Pasadena-The Woodlands, TX Metropolitan Statistical Area (CBSA 26420; OMB July 2023 delineation: Austin, Brazoria, Chambers, Fort Bend, Galveston, Harris, Liberty, Montgomery, San Jacinto and Waller counties)

electric.name: CenterPoint Energy Houston Electric
electric.serves: Regulated transmission and distribution utility (wires company) for the Greater Houston area. Its delivery charges are billed through competitive retailers. It runs the PUCT-required residential efficiency programs in its Houston Electric service territory, paying incentives through participating contractors and agencies.

electric.name: Retail electric providers (REPs), chosen by the customer
electric.serves: Households in CenterPoint's area buy electricity from a competitive retailer; offers are compared on Power to Choose, the PUCT's official electric choice site. CenterPoint's 2025 Energy Efficiency Plan describes a REP program in which participating REPs market CenterPoint's CoolSaver A/C tune-ups and the 'Efficiency Connection' online marketplace to their customers.

electric.name: Texas-New Mexico Power (TNMP)
electric.serves: Another wires utility with a Texas Gulf Coast service area. Its service-area page shows only a map, so the specific Houston-area cities could not be confirmed. TNMP runs its own Residential and Hard-to-Reach Standard Offer Programs with a 2026 program manual.

gas.name: CenterPoint Energy (natural gas, Texas divisions)
gas.serves: Natural gas distribution in its Houston, Beaumont/East Texas, Texas Coast and South Texas divisions. Rates are regulated by the Railroad Commission of Texas.

utilities.notes: Retail electric choice applies across CenterPoint Houston Electric's territory. CenterPoint delivers power and runs the efficiency programs; REPs sell the electricity. CenterPoint's incentives go to participating contractors and service providers, who apply them to the homeowner's invoice. Its solar page states 'This is not a direct-to-customer program', and its insulation page says 'The rebate is given to the contractor who may extend savings to you on your bill.' No CenterPoint residential natural-gas rebate program for Texas customers was found on CenterPoint's current site (sitemap reviewed 2026-10-12); its gas appliance rebate pages are for Minnesota and Indiana customers. Parts of the 10-county MSA are served by other utilities (TNMP, and in outer counties possibly non-choice utilities or co-ops); those were not researched in detail.

auditPrograms.name: CenterPoint Energy Agencies in Action (free home energy audit + weatherization)
auditPrograms.runBy: CenterPoint Energy Houston Electric (Targeted Low-Income Market Transformation Program), delivered by local agencies and energy service companies
auditPrograms.cost: Free: 'All energy audits and approved installations are 100% free for qualified residents.'
auditPrograms.whoQualifies: Residential customers in CenterPoint's Houston Electric service territory, living in a home at least 16 years old, who meet the income-eligibility guidelines. The page also lists receiving benefits such as SNAP, Medicare or Supplemental Security Income. Renters can take part with landlord permission. Homes with foundation, plumbing or significant sheetrock damage must fix those first. CenterPoint's 2025 plan describes eligibility as household income under 200% of federal poverty guidelines.
auditPrograms.whatYouGet: A trained professional does an in-home energy audit (air leaks, insulation levels, safety issues). An approved provider then installs the recommended upgrades at no cost: air sealing, HVAC tune-ups or upgrades, water heater pipe insulation, LED lighting, solar screens for south- and west-facing windows, low-flow showerheads, and ceiling or wall insulation. CenterPoint's 2025 plan says the audit uses DOE's NEAT tool and caps spending at $8,250 per home.
auditPrograms.howToBook: Apply via the application form on CenterPoint's Agencies in Action page, or contact a participating agency directly: Chinese Community Center, Love Network of Baytown, Peoples United Summit, Premier Center, Rebuilding Together Houston, Sustainable Services, Tejano Center, VN Teamwork.
auditPrograms.status: Open: the page carries an active application form. No 2026 funding-exhausted notice appeared on 2026-10-12.

auditPrograms.name: BakerRipley Weatherization Assistance Program (Harris County)
auditPrograms.runBy: BakerRipley (TDHCA's WAP subrecipient for Harris County), funded by DOE and HHS
auditPrograms.cost: Free: 'our services are FREE for qualifying households.'
auditPrograms.whoQualifies: Harris County residents meeting HHS income guidelines. Applicants need 30 days of income proof for all members 18+, ID for every household member, federal-benefit eligibility documents (e.g., U.S. passport, birth certificate, naturalization or permanent resident card), and current electric and gas bills.
auditPrograms.whatYouGet: Sealing around doors, windows and HVAC ducts; replacement of select appliances with ENERGY STAR models; LED bulbs; low-flow showerheads and faucets; attic and wall insulation; solar screens. Under TDHCA's statewide WAP design, work follows an energy audit.
auditPrograms.howToBook: Use BakerRipley's 'Request an Application' link, or contact the United Way of Greater Houston 211 Texas / United Way HELPLINE.
auditPrograms.status: Applications requested through the page; the page states no waitlist or closure. Separately, BakerRipley's Utility Assistance program shows 'Applications are currently closed.'

rebates.name: CenterPoint HVAC System Replacement Incentives
rebates.runBy: CenterPoint Energy Houston Electric, through participating HVAC contractors
rebates.amount: 'CenterPoint offers incentives that start at $200 and may increase, depending on your installation.' Applied directly to the installation invoice.
rebates.whoQualifies: Homes in CenterPoint's Houston Electric territory installing central A/C, heat pumps or mini-splits rated 15.2 SEER2 or higher (Texas minimum is 14.0 SEER2), installed by a participating contractor.
rebates.status: Not stated. The page shows no funding or closure notice.

rebates.name: CenterPoint ComfortCheck A/C Tune-Up Program
rebates.runBy: CenterPoint Energy Houston Electric (independent certified technicians)
rebates.amount: Not stated on the current page. CenterPoint's 2025 Energy Efficiency Plan says the program 'pays incentives to the A/C contractor to reduce the customer's upfront cost of system diagnosis and correction.'
rebates.whoQualifies: Residential customers in the Houston Electric service area (excluding apartments) with a central A/C or heat pump at least one year old and working, and no A/C tune-up through the program in the past five years.
rebates.status: Enrollment link ('Enroll Today') live on 2026-10-12; no dates or funding status stated.

rebates.name: CenterPoint Ceiling and Attic Insulation Incentives
rebates.runBy: CenterPoint Energy Houston Electric, through approved insulation contractors
rebates.amount: Not stated. 'The rebate is given to the contractor who may extend savings to you on your bill.'
rebates.whoQualifies: Existing homes in the Greater Houston area with insufficient insulation. Newly constructed homes are not eligible.
rebates.status: Not stated; no funding notice on the page.

rebates.name: CenterPoint Heat Pump Water Heater Incentive
rebates.runBy: CenterPoint Energy Houston Electric, through approved plumbing professionals
rebates.amount: Not stated: 'Incentives can vary depending on selected equipment.'
rebates.whoQualifies: Customers in CenterPoint's Houston electric territory (excluding apartments) who replace an existing residential electric storage water heater with a new ENERGY STAR certified heat pump water heater.
rebates.status: Not stated; contact CenterPoint for a list of approved plumbers.

rebates.name: CenterPoint Residential Solar Program
rebates.runBy: CenterPoint Energy Houston Electric, through participating solar service providers (PUCT-approved efficiency funding)
rebates.amount: $135/kW of rated DC system size, capped at 15 kW. Applied as a credit on the installation invoice.
rebates.whoQualifies: Existing single-family homes in the Houston Electric territory. New construction and homes with existing PV are not eligible. An interconnection agreement with CenterPoint is required.
rebates.status: Not stated; no funding notice on the page.

rebates.name: CenterPoint Variable Speed Pool Pump program
rebates.runBy: CenterPoint Energy, through participating independent contractors
rebates.amount: Not stated; the page refers customers to CenterPoint for the list of participating contractors.
rebates.whoQualifies: Pool owners; the page does not spell out eligibility.

rebates.name: City of Houston Home Repair programs (HCD)
rebates.runBy: City of Houston Housing and Community Development Department
rebates.amount: Repairs can include roofing, HVAC, windows and doors. DR24 tiers: emergency/minor under $50,000; moderate/substantial rehab $50,000.01–$80,000; gut rehab $80,000.01–$200,000; reconstruction $80,000.01–$250,000.
rebates.whoQualifies: City of Houston homeowner-occupants at or below 80% AMI, with taxes current and the home outside the floodway. Priority for seniors 62+, families with children and people with disabilities.
rebates.status: Mostly closed or paused. The general Home Repair Program has exhausted its funding and new applicant files are not being reviewed. Single-Family Home Repair is closed. Winter Storm Uri (DR21) applications are 'temporarily paused.' DR24 (derecho/Beryl) Phase 1 is closing, with no new applications 'until further notice.' Programs are suspended inside the Fifth Ward/Kashmere Gardens UPRR sampling zone.

stateHomeEnergyRebates.status: Not launched. SECO says 'Rebates are not currently available.' The programs are being designed in fall 2026, and 'A launch date has not been set and will depend on DOE approval of the final program design.'
stateHomeEnergyRebates.programName: Texas HOMES and HEAR Rebate programs (Home Efficiency Rebates, HOMES; Home Electrification and Appliance Rebates, HEAR)
stateHomeEnergyRebates.administrator: Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts, State Energy Conservation Office (SECO). Implementer: APTIM Federal Services, LLC, hired April 2026.
stateHomeEnergyRebates.summary: $690 million DOE allocation. HOMES will be open to all incomes; HEAR is limited to households below 150% of AMI (low <80%, moderate 80–150%). Amounts are not set, and HOMES levels are under DOE review. Projects finished before launch are unlikely to qualify. Funds must be spent by Sept 30, 2031.

incomeQualified.name: Weatherization Assistance Program, Harris County
incomeQualified.summary: Free DOE/HHS-funded weatherization for income-eligible Harris County residents: sealing, insulation, solar screens, ENERGY STAR appliance replacement, LEDs, low-flow fixtures. Apply via BakerRipley's application request or 211/United Way HELPLINE. BakerRipley is also TDHCA's CEAP (bill assistance) provider for Harris, Brazoria and Galveston counties.

incomeQualified.name: CenterPoint Agencies in Action
incomeQualified.runBy: CenterPoint Energy Houston Electric with local agencies
incomeQualified.summary: Free audit plus free weatherization upgrades (up to $8,250 per home per CenterPoint's 2025 plan) for income-eligible customers in homes 16+ years old in the Houston Electric territory.

incomeQualified.name: CenterPoint Hard-to-Reach Standard Offer Program
incomeQualified.runBy: CenterPoint Energy Houston Electric, through registered project sponsors (contractors)
incomeQualified.summary: Contractor-delivered incentives for HVAC replacement, duct sealing, weatherization, ceiling insulation, water-saving measures and ENERGY STAR windows for customers with household income below 200% of federal poverty guidelines. Described in CenterPoint's 2025 Energy Efficiency Plan and Report (PUCT Project 57468), which says no additional programs were planned for 2026. Current-year status was not published on a customer page.

incomeQualified.name: WAP providers for the rest of the Houston MSA
incomeQualified.summary: Fort Bend and Austin counties: Combined Community Action, Inc. Montgomery and Waller: Brazos Valley Community Action Programs. Brazoria: Crossroads Community Action. Galveston, Liberty, Chambers and San Jacinto: Greater East Texas Community Action Program (GETCAP).

incomeQualified.name: City of Houston Home Repair
incomeQualified.runBy: City of Houston Housing and Community Development Department
incomeQualified.summary: Repairs for homeowners at or below 80% AMI (roof, HVAC, windows/doors and more). Funding is currently exhausted or applications paused for nearly all tracks. Questions: 832-394-6200 or homerepair@houstontx.gov.

localRules.name: No energy audit, disclosure-at-sale or benchmarking mandate for private buildings in Houston
localRules.summary: No City of Houston requirement for home energy audits, disclosure at sale or private-building benchmarking was found. ACEEE's State & Local Policy Database (non-government source, sections last updated Sept 2023 to Feb 2024) reports only a voluntary commercial benchmarking program run with Better Buildings. It also notes a 2022 Municipal Building Decarbonization and Benchmarking Policy that 'applies to municipal and city-operated buildings.' Ordinary homeowners have no audit or disclosure obligation.

notes: Federal home-efficiency tax credits are over. The IRS says the 25C credit 'will not be allowed for any property placed in service after December 31, 2025', and the 25D credit is not allowed for expenditures after Dec 31, 2025. Texas HOMES/HEAR rebates have not launched. CenterPoint's site was redesigned in 2026: older program URLs (e.g., /SaveEnergyandMoney/ pages and the Residential Efficiency Programs page) now 404 or redirect to an article. Only the pages cited here were confirmed live on 2026-10-12, and CenterPoint publishes few dollar amounts on them (HVAC 'starts at $200'; solar $135/kW). The A/C tune-up is now branded 'ComfortCheck'; CenterPoint's 2025 plan calls it CoolSaver. CenterPoint's High Efficiency Homes program pays builders for new ENERGY STAR or above-code homes, which matters to buyers of new homes, not to existing homeowners. No City of Houston audit or efficiency rebate program for market-rate homeowners was found, and the City's Green Houston climate site blocked automated access. Unverified: current 2026 funding levels for CenterPoint programs (the 2026 Energy Efficiency Plan filing was not located); any Texas natural-gas efficiency rebates from CenterPoint; exactly which Houston-area cities TNMP serves; WAP waitlist length at BakerRipley.
